context: Bivariate (actually trivariate) treemap encoding revenue as area, category as color (6 hues), subcategory as pattern shape (6 types × 24 subcategories), and growth rate as pattern density (spacing). ~60-80 leaf nodes across 6 categories and 24 subcategories. No animation; hover tooltip for detail.
first_impression: The category-color blocks read immediately, but the layered pattern encoding creates visual noise that obscures rather than informs.
what_works: The 6-color Tol palette cleanly separates categories even at small cell sizes; category header labels and padding make the treemap hierarchy legible at a glance. The density gradient legend is a nice design touch.
what_doesnt: Pattern density (growth rate) is nearly imperceptible in small cells and indistinguishable across the range — the channel is too subtle to decode without hovering every cell. Pattern shape encodes subcategory but 6 patterns map to 24 subcategories, so the same pattern (e.g. diagonal hatch) represents different subcategories in different color regions, making the encoding unreliable and the legend misleading.
